source.test: scanServerDirectory + detectJavaFlavor (no jar, no bedrock binary at all)

notes: scanServerDirectory never rejects or errors on a directory with no launch artifact at all: hasJar and hasBedrock are both false, so `(hasBedrock && !hasJar)` is false and .java is selected by default (line 246); detectJavaFlavor then falls through every signature to the Paper case with `jars` empty, giving javaFlavor "paper" with a null jar/version rather than an unknown/error state. fixtures/paper-import/rejects-directory-without-java-jar.json (Phase 4) looks like it contradicts this, but it doesn't: that fixture characterizes a different function, import_existing_paper_server (crates/msc-application/src/import.rs) — Phase 4's own narrower, registration-only Rust function, which deliberately rejects a jar-less directory as new Rust-side validation, not a port of scanServerDirectory. Its source pointer previously mis-attributed that validation to scanServerDirectory; corrected in that fixture directly. This raw-import scan path (P5.19's oracle) genuinely never rejects, per MSC 1's real scanServerDirectory.
